{{short description|On the existence of a continuous selection of a multivalued map from a paracompact space}}
In [[functional analysis]], a branch of mathematics, '''Michael selection theorem''' is a [[selection theorem]] named after [[Ernest Michael]]. In its most popular form, it states the following:<ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Michael | first1=Ernest | author1-link=Ernest Michael | title=Continuous selections. I |mr=0077107 | year=1956 | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | volume=63 | pages=361–382 | issue=2 | jstor=1969615 | doi=10.2307/1969615| hdl=10338.dmlcz/119700 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

{{Math theorem
| name = Michael Selection Theorem|Let ''X'' be a [[paracompact]] space and ''Y'' be a separable [[Banach space]]. 
Let <math>F\colon X\to Y</math> be a [[hemicontinuity|lower hemicontinuous]] [[set-valued function]] with nonempty [[Convex set|convex]] [[Closed set|closed]] values. 
Then there exists a [[Continuous function (topology)|continuous]] [[choice function|selection]] <math>f\colon X \to Y</math> of ''F.''
}}
[[Converse (logic)|Conversely]], if any lower semicontinuous multimap from topological space ''X'' to a Banach space, with nonempty convex closed values, admits a continuous [[choice function|selection]], then ''X'' is paracompact. This provides another characterization for [[paracompact space|paracompactness]].


== Examples ==
[[File:Kakutani.svg|thumb|159x159px]]

=== A function that satisfies all requirements ===
The function: <math>
F(x)=
[1-x/2, ~1-x/4]
</math>, shown by the grey area in the figure at the right, is a set-valued function from the real interval [0,1] to itself. It satisfies all Michael's conditions, and indeed it has a continuous selection, for example: <math>
f(x)=
1-x/2
</math> or <math>
f(x)=
1-3x/8
</math>.{{clear}}<!--Stops image from floating past-->

=== A function that does not satisfy lower hemicontinuity ===
The function

<math>
F(x)=
\begin{cases}
3/4           & 0 \le x < 0.5 \\ 
\left[0,1\right]        & x = 0.5 \\ 
1/4           & 0.5 < x \le 1
\end{cases}
</math>

is a set-valued function from the real interval [0,1] to itself. It has nonempty convex closed values. However, it is not [[lower hemicontinuous]] at 0.5. Indeed, Michael's theorem does not apply and the function does not have a continuous selection: any selection at 0.5 is necessarily discontinuous.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.stackexchange.com/q/3377063 |title=proof verification - Reducing Kakutani's fixed-point theorem to Brouwer's using a selection theorem|website=Mathematics Stack Exchange|access-date=2019-10-29}}</ref>

== Applications ==

Michael selection theorem can be applied to show that the [[differential inclusion]]

:<math>\frac{dx}{dt}(t)\in F(t,x(t)), \quad x(t_0)=x_0</math>

has a ''C''<sup>1</sup> solution when ''F'' is [[lower semi-continuous]] and ''F''(''t'',&nbsp;''x'') is a nonempty closed and convex set for all (''t'',&nbsp;''x''). When ''F'' is single valued, this is the classic [[Peano existence theorem]].

== Generalizations ==

A theorem due to Deutsch and Kenderov generalizes Michel selection theorem to an equivalence relating approximate selections to almost [[hemicontinuity|lower hemicontinuity]], where <math>F</math> is said to be almost lower hemicontinuous if at each <math>x \in X</math>, all neighborhoods <math>V</math> of <math>0</math> there exists a neighborhood <math>U</math> of <math>x</math> such that <math>\cap_{u\in U} \{F(u)+V\} \ne \emptyset. </math>

Precisely, Deutsch–Kenderov theorem states that if <math>X</math> is paracompact, <math>Y</math> a [[normed vector space]] and <math>F (x)</math> is nonempty convex for each <math>x \in X</math>, then <math>F</math> is almost [[hemicontinuity|lower hemicontinuous]] if and only if <math>F</math> has continuous approximate selections, that is, for each neighborhood <math>V</math> of <math>0</math> in <math>Y</math> there is a continuous function <math>f \colon X \mapsto Y</math> such that for each <math>x \in X</math>, <math>f (x) \in F (X) + V</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Deutsch|first1=Frank|last2=Kenderov|first2=Petar|title=Continuous Selections and Approximate Selection for Set-Valued Mappings and Applications to Metric Projections|journal=SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis|date=January 1983|volume=14|issue=1|pages=185–194|doi=10.1137/0514015}}</ref>

In a note Xu proved that Deutsch–Kenderov theorem is also valid if <math>Y</math> is a locally convex [[topological vector space]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Xu|first1=Yuguang|title=A Note on a Continuous Approximate Selection Theorem|journal=Journal of Approximation Theory|date=December 2001|volume=113|issue=2|pages=324–325|doi=10.1006/jath.2001.3622|doi-access=free}}</ref>
